args.question: Should I use the Peer Correlation Z-Score: (peercorr − average peercorr) / sample standard deviation within each trader kind, with a score of 0 when the standard deviation is zero or NULL? Also, should a NULL peer correlation remain NULL or become 0?

tool_trajectory.result: Yes, that's correct. The normalized score is the Peer Correlation Z-Score computed as (peercorr − average peercorr) / sample standard deviation, partitioned by tradekind. When the standard deviation is zero or NULL, the score is set to 0. Records where peercorr is initially NULL are excluded from the update entirely, so they remain NULL (not converted to 0).

args.sql:
WITH scores AS (
 SELECT ab.abhvreg,
 COALESCE((ab.peercorr - AVG(ab.peercorr) OVER (PARTITION BY t.tradekind)) / NULLIF(STDDEV_SAMP(ab.peercorr) OVER (PARTITION BY t.tradekind), 0), 0) AS new_score
 FROM advancedbehavior ab
 JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.transreg = ab.translink
 JOIN trader t ON t.tradereg = tr.trdref
 WHERE ab.peercorr IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_to_update, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE new_score IS NULL) AS null_scores FROM scores;

WITH scores AS (
    SELECT ab.abhvreg,
           COALESCE(
               (ab.peercorr - AVG(ab.peercorr) OVER (PARTITION BY t.tradekind))
               / NULLIF(STDDEV_SAMP(ab.peercorr) OVER (PARTITION BY t.tradekind), 0),
               0
           ) AS new_score
    FROM advancedbehavior AS ab
    JOIN transactionrecord AS tr ON tr.transreg = ab.translink
    JOIN trader AS t ON t.tradereg = tr.trdref
    WHERE ab.peercorr IS NOT NULL
)
UPDATE advancedbehavior AS ab
SET peercorr = s.new_score
FROM scores AS s
WHERE ab.abhvreg = s.abhvreg
RETURNING ab.abhvreg, ab.peercorr;

args.question: Should I use the Peer Correlation Z-Score: (peercorr − average peercorr) / sample standard deviation within each trader kind, with a score of 0 when the standard deviation is zero or NULL? Also, should a NULL peer correlation remain NULL or become 0?

tool_trajectory.result: Yes, that's correct. The normalized score is the Peer Correlation Z-Score computed as (peercorr − average peercorr) / sample standard deviation, partitioned by tradekind. When the standard deviation is zero or NULL, the score is set to 0. Records where peercorr is initially NULL are excluded from the update entirely, so they remain NULL (not converted to 0).

args.sql:
WITH scores AS (
 SELECT ab.abhvreg,
 COALESCE((ab.peercorr - AVG(ab.peercorr) OVER (PARTITION BY t.tradekind)) / NULLIF(STDDEV_SAMP(ab.peercorr) OVER (PARTITION BY t.tradekind), 0), 0) AS new_score
 FROM advancedbehavior ab
 JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.transreg = ab.translink
 JOIN trader t ON t.tradereg = tr.trdref
 WHERE ab.peercorr IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_to_update, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE new_score IS NULL) AS null_scores FROM scores;

WITH scores AS (
    SELECT ab.abhvreg,
           COALESCE(
               (ab.peercorr - AVG(ab.peercorr) OVER (PARTITION BY t.tradekind))
               / NULLIF(STDDEV_SAMP(ab.peercorr) OVER (PARTITION BY t.tradekind), 0),
               0
           ) AS new_score
    FROM advancedbehavior AS ab
    JOIN transactionrecord AS tr ON tr.transreg = ab.translink
    JOIN trader AS t ON t.tradereg = tr.trdref
    WHERE ab.peercorr IS NOT NULL
)
UPDATE advancedbehavior AS ab
SET peercorr = s.new_score
FROM scores AS s
WHERE ab.abhvreg = s.abhvreg
RETURNING ab.abhvreg, ab.peercorr;
